answer: Each agent must lock a deposit before it can submit a signed claim, and the protocol randomly selects claims for costly audits against independently observed outcomes. A proven false claim burns the deposit and excludes the signing key; honest claims recover the stake after review. This does not make identities unique, but it makes each additional Sybil costly: an attacker must fund many deposits and risks losing them when audited. A reef report, comet sighting, or jade shipment can all be checked under the same rule.
